what_its_for: Testosterone cypionate is used to treat low testosterone levels in men (a condition called hypogonadism). It replaces or supplements the testosterone that your body is not making enough of on its own. It may also be used for other conditions as determined by your doctor.
how_to_take: This medication is given as an injection into the muscle (usually the buttock or thigh). It is most often given by a healthcare provider in a clinic or doctor's office. If your doctor teaches you to give it to yourself at home, follow their instructions carefully. Always use a new, sterile needle and syringe for each injection. Never share needles or syringes with anyone else. Rotate injection sites to avoid soreness or lumps under the skin.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your testosterone blood levels and how you respond to treatment. A common starting dose is 50 to 400 mg injected every 2 to 4 weeks, but your dose may be different. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to check your levels and may adjust your dose over time. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a scheduled injection, contact your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not try to make up a missed dose by doubling your next dose. Your doctor will advise you on the best time to give your next injection based on your schedule.
storage: Store testosterone cypionate at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not refrigerate or freeze the medication. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Check the solution before each use — it should be clear to slightly yellow with no particles. If it looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles, do not use it and contact your pharmacist. Dispose of used needles and syringes in an approved sharps container right away.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol while taking this medication, as it can lower testosterone levels and cause liver problems. Do not share this medication with anyone else — it is prescribed only for you and sharing it is illegal. Avoid applying the injection solution to your skin or letting others come into contact with it. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should avoid touching this medication, as it can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you use any supplements, especially those marketed for bodybuilding or muscle gain.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, or trouble breathing (possible signs of a blood clot or heart problem); sudden severe headache, vision changes, or weakness on one side of the body (possible stroke symptoms); painful, prolonged erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism); signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; swelling of the ankles or feet; mood changes, depression, or increased aggression; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or severe stomach pain; sleep apnea (loud snoring or pauses in breathing while asleep); or any unusual lumps, pain, or hardness at the injection site.
when_it_works: Many men begin to notice improvements in energy, mood, and sex drive within 3 to 6 weeks of starting treatment. Full benefits such as improved muscle strength, reduced body fat, and better bone density may take 3 to 6 months or longer to develop. Your doctor will monitor your testosterone levels with blood tests, usually a few weeks after starting or adjusting your dose, to make sure the medication is working properly.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution. Older men may have a higher risk of heart problems, prostate issues, or other side effects. Your doctor will monitor you more closely. Children and teenagers: Testosterone cypionate is not approved for use in children unless specifically directed by a specialist. It can affect growth and development. Women: This medication is generally not recommended for women except in very specific medical situations determined by a doctor. Pregnant women must not use this medication as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Men with prostate cancer or breast cancer: Do not use this medication. Men with heart disease, kidney disease, or liver disease: Use with extra caution. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions before starting this medication.
